transcript.text:
I can help with that. A washing machine refusing to spin usually comes down to one of two things: either the load inside has become unbalanced (the machine pauses to redistribute heavy items like towels or a duvet), or it cannot drain the water first because it won't spin until the drum is empty. To narrow this down, please run a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme. While it runs, listen near the bottom front of the machine:
1. Can you hear the pump humming or running?
2. Is the water actually draining out into the waste pipe? Let me know what happens with both the sound and the water flow.
it drained fine, no water left in the drum. its just the one thing came out dripping, a big bath mat. didnt try a drain programme tho, do i need to?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. You don't need to run a separate drain programme since you've confirmed there's no water left in the drum. The fact that it drained fine but won't spin with just one big bath mat is classic unbalanced-load behaviour. When a single heavy item like a bath mat soaks up all the water, it sticks to one side of the drum. The machine detects this imbalance and refuses to spin at high speed because the weight would make it bang around dangerously. It may try to tumble slowly back and forth to redistribute it, but often gives up. Please open the door, take out that bath mat and shake it out so it isn't stuck to one side. Add a couple of smaller items like towels or t-shirts to help balance it, then close the door and try running just the 'Spin' programme again.
ok will try it with the mat plus a couple of towels. what do i do after that?

Run the Spin programme. If it spins normally with that mix of items, then it was just the bath mat causing an imbalance and your machine is fine. If it still refuses to spin or keeps trying to redistribute without success, please let me know exactly what happens (does it stay silent, make a humming noise, or bang around?). That will tell us if we need to look at the motor or suspension.
tried it with the mat plus a couple of towels and it spun up fine. mat came out damp not dripping. so is it ok?

Yes, it is perfectly ok. Your washing machine is fine; the issue was simply that single heavy bath mat causing an imbalance, which is a normal safety feature to prevent damage. To stop this happening again, try not to wash one very heavy item on its own. If you must wash something like a bath mat or duvet cover, add a couple of towels or similar items to help balance the weight in the drum. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
